name: Nishânî
bio: Nishani, Jelal-Zade Mustafa, was the great historian of Suleyman's reign and held some of the highest offices of state, among them that of Nishanji, Cipher-writer to the Sultan.
The poems here are taken from E. J. W. Gibb's Ottoman Poems (1882), the first English verse translations of Ottoman poetry; dates and biographical details follow Gibb's Biographical Notices.

poems.title: I Began Love's Art to Study
poems.author: Nishânî
poems.text:
I began love's art to study, divers chapters did I read;
Longing's texts and parting's sections, a whole book would fill indeed

Union formed a short abridgment, but the pangs of love for thee
Have their commentaries endless made each other to succeed.

O Nishânî, hath the master, Love, thus truly taught to thee: —
"This a question hard whose answer from the loved one must proceed!"
